meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'hello'.

examples.trans: Hello, Elena Vladimirovna.
Hello, Arkady Borisovich!
Hello! How are you?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The rookie has returned!
I know that you are pregnant!
The main thing is that I am here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'my', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Но я точно знаю, что ребёнок мой.
examples.trans: But I know for sure that the child is mine.

examples.text: Дело в том, что это мой ребёнок.
examples.trans: The thing is that this is my child.
My first husband is Victor Petrovich.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'wife' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Is Den married?
His wife left him.
My wife is being monitored by you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'блюдаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'is being monitored / seen'.

related.gloss: not to is being monitored (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и наблюдаться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and is being monitored on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют наблюдаться.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to is being monitored.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, near, with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do not drink anything for a minute!
The rookie has returned!
We need to talk!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Are you two chatting here?

examples.text: А я вот себе туфли новые купил.
examples.trans: And I just bought myself new shoes.

examples.text: Вы с Викой расстались, и она сразу кого-то нашла?
examples.trans: You and Vika broke up, and she immediately found someone?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'she', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: She is a good one you have.
Calm down, I will leave everything to a professional.
Maybe she was joking?

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'сить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'asked for', paired with 'попросить'.

examples.text: Она просила меня забрать её анализы.
examples.trans: She asked me to pick up her test results.

examples.text: А меня Виктория просила ничего не говорить.
examples.trans: And Victoria asked me not to say anything.

examples.text: Познакомь, а то мне придётся Катю просить.
examples.trans: Introduce us, or else I will have to ask Katya.

meanings.en: to take away, to pick up
meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'брать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to take away', paired with 'забирать'.

examples.text: Она просила меня забрать её анализы.
examples.trans: She asked me to pick up her test results.
He will withdraw the statement.
I'll take the keys.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'test results / analyses' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Она просила меня забрать её анализы.
examples.trans: She asked me to pick up her test results.
Remember your last test.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Eleonora had an unhappy marriage.
In a divorce, two people are always at fault.

examples.text: Даже не знаешь человека и защищаешь его.
examples.trans: You do not even know the man and you defend him.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Vika, wait!
We need to talk!
I know that you are pregnant!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I know that you are pregnant!
The main thing is that I am here.

examples.text: Тем более, что ты уже начал.
examples.trans: Especially since you have already started.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nothing', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do not drink anything for a minute!

examples.text: Почему ты ничего мне не рассказывал?
examples.trans: Why did you not tell me anything?

examples.text: Слушай, Эля, ты думаешь, я ничего не понимаю?
examples.trans: Listen, Elya, do you think I understand nothing?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do not drink anything for a minute!

examples.text: Не важно, кто мне это сказал.
examples.trans: It does not matter who told me this.
This is not your child.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to speak', paired with 'сказать'.

examples.trans: We need to talk!
Go to our place, we will talk tonight.

examples.text: Моя бывшая беременна, говорит, что не от меня.
examples.trans: My ex is pregnant and says it is not mine.

examples.text: Даже не знаешь человека и защищаешь его.

examples.trans: Vika, wait!

examples.trans: Let's find out the name of our grand winner!

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'forgive', paired with 'прощать'.

examples.trans: Forgive me, this is very important.
Lena, forgive me.
I am at fault, forgive me.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Не важно, кто мне это сказал.
examples.trans: It does not matter who told me this.

examples.text: Я готов быть отцом этого ребёнка.
examples.trans: I am ready to be the father of this child.
This is not your child.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'very', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Почему ты ничего мне не рассказывал?
examples.trans: Why did you not tell me anything?
Do you want to ruin our relationship?

examples.text: Если ты не хочешь, я не буду тебя заставлять.
examples.trans: If you do not want to, I will not force you.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important, mattering').

examples.text: Не важно, кто мне это сказал.
examples.trans: It does not matter who told me this.
Forgive me, this is very important.
This is important for your career.

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to
meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: We need to talk!
I need to know the truth.

examples.text: Ему нужна мама для его дочки.
examples.trans: He needs a mother for his daughter.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know'.

examples.trans: I know that you are pregnant!

examples.text: Я узнала о тебе много нового.
examples.trans: I learned a lot of new things about you.

examples.text: Даже не знаешь человека и защищаешь его.

examples.text: Моя команда справится с послом и без меня.
examples.trans: My team will handle the ambassador without me.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, am able to', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.trans: I can't today.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: Who told you?

examples.text: Не важно, кто мне это сказал.
examples.trans: It does not matter who told me this.

examples.trans: On that day when you refused to marry me.

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'child / baby' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я готов быть отцом этого ребёнка.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').

examples.trans: Please, hear me out.
Come back, excuse me, please.
A coffee, please.

meanings.en: to hear out, listen attentively to
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'слушать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to listen to, hear out', paired with 'выслушивать'.

examples.trans: Please, hear me out.
First listen to me very carefully.
The judge patiently heard out the witness's testimony.
